problem: The text says there are isolators before and after the doped fiber, but the block diagram shows only one isolator, placed after the erbium-doped fiber. A student comparing the two will think one isolator is missing.
fix: Either add an input isolator node between the WDM coupler and the erbium-doped fiber, or change the text to say an isolator after the doped fiber blocks backward ASE and reflections (with a second isolator at the input in some designs).

problem: The question mentions a 10 dB span loss, then gives an amplifier input of −18 dBm. The answer uses −18 dBm as the amplifier input, so the 10 dB never enters the calculation. A student may read −18 dBm as the power at the start of the span and get −5 dBm.
fix: State the input clearly: 'the power entering the amplifier is −18 dBm' (the 10 dB span loss has already been accounted for), so output = −18 + 23 = +5 dBm.

problem: 'The erbium gain medium has no carrier-density noise' is not the standard reason, and it is vague. The EDFA noise figure is low because 980 nm pumping gives almost complete population inversion, so the spontaneous-emission factor is close to 1, plus low excess loss; an SOA has incomplete inversion and higher internal loss, giving a larger spontaneous-emission factor and NF of 6-8 dB.
fix: The erbium gain medium is almost fully inverted, so it adds close to the minimum spontaneous emission (NF about 3-5 dB), while the SOA's incomplete inversion and higher loss give NF 6-8 dB.
